beats.narration: First thing it hands you is the shopping list. Every dish has its own ingredients, and CostCook rolls them all up into one list, scaled to two hundred. Red onion is in the pilaf and in the salad. Here it's one line. Just over fifteen pounds. One bag, twenty-five pounds. The list is grouped by supplier, in packs you can actually buy. Three cases of chicken thigh from Sysco. Five cases of pita from the bakery. Each stop gets its own subtotal, so you know what you're spending before you walk in. And down here, the honest number. About nine hundred dollars out the door, seven eighty-five in what the food itself costs. The gap is pack round-up. This list used to be my whole evening. Now it's done before the coffee's poured.
